user_text: Summarize the benefits of code review for a small team.
assistant_text:
# Benefits of Code Review for a Small Team

## Quality & Reliability
- **Catches bugs early** before they reach production, reducing costly fixes later
- **Enforces consistency** in coding style and standards across the codebase

## Knowledge Sharing
- **Spreads expertise** so no single person is the only one who understands a feature
- **Onboards new members faster** by exposing them to existing patterns and practices

## Collaboration & Communication
- **Encourages discussion** around design decisions and trade-offs
- **Builds a shared sense of ownership** over the codebase

## Risk Reduction
- **Reduces the "bus factor"** — the risk of losing critical knowledge if someone leaves
- **Provides a second set of eyes** to spot security vulnerabilities or edge cases

## Continuous Improvement
- **Promotes learning** as developers give and receive constructive feedback
- **Gradually improves team standards** over time

---

## Practical Tips for Small Teams
- Keep reviews **short and focused** (under 400 lines at a time)
- Set a **clear turnaround time** (e.g., within 24 hours) to avoid blocking work
- Use a **lightweight checklist** to keep reviews consistent without being burdensome

> Even with a team of 2–3 people, regular code review pays dividends in long-term maintainability and team cohesion.
Code review helps small teams catch bugs early, share knowledge, and maintain a consistent, high-quality codebase.

1. **Bug detection** – A second set of eyes catches errors before they reach production.
2. **Knowledge sharing** – Team members learn from each other, reducing reliance on any single person.
Code review builds a **shared sense of ownership**, encouraging team members to collectively take pride and responsibility in the codebase rather than treating code as individually "owned."

user_text: State one risk if reviews are skipped.
assistant_text: If reviews are skipped, critical knowledge can become siloed with one developer, creating a **"bus factor"** risk where the team is severely impacted if that person leaves or is unavailable.
Track **defect escape rate** — the number of bugs found in production versus those caught during review — to measure how effectively code reviews are improving quality over time.
Consistent code review is a small investment that pays off in fewer bugs, stronger teamwork, and a healthier codebase.

• Code review catches bugs early and improves quality.
• It spreads knowledge and reduces single points of failure.
• It builds team ownership and collaboration.
• Skipping it risks siloed knowledge and escaped defects.
• Track defect escape rate to measure its effectiveness.
• Even a lightweight process delivers long-term value.
Code review is a simple practice that keeps code quality high, knowledge shared, and teams working well together.
Code review is only effective if feedback is constructive and timely — overly critical or delayed reviews can slow progress and harm team morale.
Bad or slow reviews can hurt productivity and team morale.
Code review boosts quality and collaboration, but only works well when feedback is timely, constructive, and consistent.
